newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 15.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Prices paid to American manufacturers and other producers fell 0.6 percent in April, possibly making it harder for the Federal Reserve to justify a further rate tightening next week.
* The distribution methods of Philip Morris Cos Inc is under investigation by the Federal Trade Commission.
* Legal attacks against Intel Corp are a headache, but unlikely to cause serious damage to the company, according to analysts and lawyers.
* SBC Warburg is expected to announce an agreement to buy the Wall Street investment banking firm of Dillon, Read & Co for about $600 million.
* The lawyer who represented New York Yankees owner George Steinbrenner in a lawsuit against Major League Baseball has quit the law firm.
* General Motors Corp has reached a tentative agreement with workers at an Ohio components plant.
* A federal regulatory agency has withheld approval of the merger of Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power Co.
* Hoffmann-La Roche Inc, a unit of Roche Holding Ltd has had its obesity drug recommended for approval by a Food and Drug Administration advisory panel.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission is increasing its scrutiny of mutual-fund advice newsletters.
* California regulators are investigating GTE Corp for allegedly destroying or withholding documents that are part of a false-billing probe.
* New warning labels are about to grace packs of cigarettes on brands produced by Liggett Group, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd .
* Headhunter David Beirne of Ramsey/Beirne has left to join Benchmark Parnters, a venture-capital firm.
* General Motors Corp and AvtoVAZ, Russia's largest car market, have plans for three projects that they say could lead to the production of up to 250,000 cars in Russia.
* A proposal by Britain's Labor government to ban tobacco advertisements raises provocative questions in the debate over such ads in the U.S.
* Sun Television and Appliances Inc plans to disclose its operational and marketing overhaul to address its faltering sales.
* Heard on the Street: One of Wall Street's most prominent bulls, PaineWebber strategist Edward Kerschner, has pulled in his horns.

* Credit Markets: Remarkably benign inflation data spurred a bond rally as more investors became convinced that the Federal Reserve will hold off on an interest-rate increase at its next policy meeting on Tuesday. And if today's economic data are equally impressive, bonds could rally still further, traders predicted.
